title: Square a skewed stack of loose sheets on both axes and secure it with a binder clip
instruction: Square up the stack of paper so that all its edges are flush, and fasten it with the binder clip on the middle of one short edge. Then let go and move both arms away.
context: The pile starts uneven along both pairs of edges. Bring the pages flush, keep them together while opening the clip, and leave the whole stack secure enough to lift by the clip. A clip can grip only the top pages even when it looks correctly placed.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist. Wooden table top 1100 x 1300. Nothing else is on it. 1) Paper: 36 loose sheets of US Letter copy paper (215.9 x 279.4, 20 lb bond, 75 g/m2, about 0.1 thick and 4.5 g each; together 3.6 thick, 163 g), lying flat on top of the two reams (2), long sides along y. The stack is skewed: it is laid down as nine groups of four sheets, bottom group first, each group shifted and turned from the stack's nominal middle (628, -100) by (shift along x, shift along y, turn about the vertical, anticlockwise seen from above): (-3, +6, +2.0 deg), (+4, -6, -1.5), (-4, +7, +1.0), (+3, -5, -2.5), (-2, +4, +1.5), (+4, -7, -1.0), (-3, +6, +2.5), (+3, -4, -2.0), (-4, +5, +1.0). Measured as under scoring, the start is 18 out of flush on the long sides and 20 on the short sides. The nominal near long edge is at x 520, 50 out over the reams' near face; the short ends overhang the reams by 32 on each side. 2) Two unopened 500-sheet reams of the same Letter copy paper in their wrappers (each 279.4 x 215.9 x 51, 2.3 kg), one squarely on the other, their long side pointing away from the robot: together 279 (x) x 216 (y) x 102 high, x 570 to 849, y -208 to 8. They are taped to the table and do not move. 3) Binder clip: medium, 32 mm (1-1/4 in) wide, 5/8 in capacity, black spring steel with two wire handles, about 9 g; back 16 wide, jaws 21 deep, handles reaching 28 behind the back. It is clipped onto the top edge of its stand's fin, jaws down, both handles folded back so that they stand up and apart (33 between their ends), ready to be squeezed; its width runs along x; the middle of its back is at (250, 300, 35). 4) Clip stand: clear acrylic fin, 40 long (x) x 3 thick x 35 high, fixed upright at (250, 300) on a flat acrylic foot 60 x 40 x 3 (any rigid 3 mm sheet stood upright and taped down does). There are no marks, stops or guides on the table: the stack can only be squared between the grippers and against the table top. The layout is the same in every trial. In the overhead policy image (320 x 176) the stack is about 51 x 28 pixels, its 18 to 20 mm skew 2 to 3 pixels, the clip 6 pixels; the wrist cameras see them larger once a gripper is near. Sizes of the clip's parts, the clip's spring (about 8 N on the stack) and all friction are estimates to be measured on the bought items (TECHNICAL.md).
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial (the run limit, or as soon as the robot has let go with the 1.0 conditions met) from a photo, with a steel rule and one lift test. Let go: for the last 2 s no part of the robot has touched the paper or the clip and both gripper centre points have been at least 50 mm from them. Clamped: a sheet lies between the clip's shut jaws, the middle of their lips at least 3 mm in from the sheet's edge. Lift test (by the referee after the end, not by the robot; only if let go): the clip is taken by its back and lifted until the whole stack hangs from it, its lowest corner 152 mm above the table (50 mm above the reams), and held 2 s. Held sheets: after a lift test, the sheets still clamped that slid no more than 3 mm under the lips (a sheet that slid shows as a step at the stack's edges); without one (not let go), the sheets clamped. Flush, read before the lift test: on the clipped stack, measure on each of its four sides the step between the sheet edge that sticks out most and the one that sits back most; take the larger of the two long sides and the larger of the two short sides. Clip placed: the clip is on a short edge (its jaws point along the long side within 25 degrees) and the middle of its lips is within 20 mm of the middle of that edge. 0 for the whole trial if a sheet ever leaves the table (a corner beyond the table's edge or more than 30 mm below its top). Count only full-size sheets lying unfolded in the clipped stack. Temporary fanning while jogging the stack is allowed. Otherwise 1.0: let go, all 36 sheets held, both flush values at most 2 mm, clip placed. 0.6: let go, all 36 sheets held, both flush values at most 6 mm. 0.3: at least 18 sheets held. 0: anything else, including nothing done. Possible scores: 0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0. In simulation the 36 sheets are nine rigid plates of four, each counting as four sheets. Which hand does what, how the stack is squared and where it is left are not scored.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the clip off and park it on its fin, jaws down, handles folded back. Lay the 36 sheets back on the reams in nine groups of four, bottom group first, each set to 1 mm with a square off the reams' faces (README.md lists every group's two near corners), the long edge 50 mm over the reams' near face. Replace any creased sheet. Arms to ready, grippers open. In simulation: seed 0, zero object jitter; every plate and both halves of the clip are returned to their start poses and the scorer starts fresh.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz/20 Hz. 36 sheets = nine loose rigid plates of four (0.4 mm, 18 g, friction 0.30/0.25): no bending, curl, creasing or slip inside a plate. Reams: one fixed box. Clip: two rigid halves on a sprung hinge, handles rigid, fixed folded back; squeezing them opens it by contact alone; it grips by friction; no software rule. No intra-plate folds; lift test performed by the scorer after the end. Friction and spring estimated; no hardware trial.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2400 steps; scripted: 1.0 in 1435. Recorded state checked against the revised rubric.
